cues.en: How do you explain when things don't go as we assume? Or better,
cues.zh: 当事情的发展不如我们所料时，你如何解释？或者更确切地说，

cues.en: how do you explain
cues.zh: 你如何解释

cues.en: when others are able to achieve things that seem to defy all of the assumptions?
cues.zh: 当别人能够做到那些似乎违背所有假设的事情时？

cues.en: For example,
cues.zh: 比如说，

cues.en: why is Apple so innovative?
cues.zh: 为什么苹果如此具有创新力？

cues.en: Year after year after year after year, they're more innovative than all their competition.
cues.zh: 年复一年，年复一年，他们比所有竞争对手都更有创新力。

cues.en: And yet, they're just a computer company. They're just like everyone else. They have the same access to the same talent, the same agencies, the same consultants, the same media.
cues.zh: 然而，他们只是一家电脑公司。他们和其他人一样。他们能接触到同样的人才、同样的代理机构、同样的顾问、同样的媒体。

cues.en: Then why is it that they seem to have something different?
cues.zh: 那为什么他们似乎拥有一些不同的东西？

cues.en: Why is it that Martin Luther King led the civil rights movement?
cues.zh: 为什么是马丁·路德·金领导了民权运动？

cues.en: He wasn't the only man who suffered in a pre civil rights America,
cues.zh: 他并不是在民权运动之前的美国唯一遭受苦难的人，

cues.en: and he certainly wasn't the only great orator of the day, why him?
cues.zh: 他也肯定不是当时唯一伟大的演说家，为什么是他？

cues.en: And why is it that the Wright brothers were able to figure out controlled powered man flight when there were certainly other teams who were better qualified, better funded,
cues.zh: 为什么是莱特兄弟能够实现可控的动力载人飞行，而当时肯定有其他团队更有资格、资金更充足，

cues.en: and they didn't achieve
cues.zh: 他们却没有实现

cues.en: powered man flight, and the Wright brothers beat them to it.
cues.zh: 动力载人飞行，而莱特兄弟抢先做到了。

cues.en: There's something else at play here.
cues.zh: 这里面还有别的因素在起作用。

cues.en: About
cues.zh: 大约

cues.en: three and a half years ago, I made a discovery,
cues.zh: 三年半前，我有了一个发现，

cues.en: and this discovery profoundly changed
cues.zh: 而这个发现深刻地改变了

cues.en: my view
cues.zh: 我的看法

cues.en: on how I thought the world worked, and it even profoundly changed the way in which I operate in it.
cues.zh: 改变了我对世界如何运作的看法，它甚至深刻地改变了我在这世界上的行事方式。

cues.en: As it turns out,
cues.zh: 事实证明，

cues.en: there's a pattern. As it turns out, all the great and inspiring leaders
cues.zh: 存在一种模式。事实证明，所有伟大而鼓舞人心的领袖

cues.en: organizations in the world, whether it's Apple or Martin Luther King or the Wright brothers, they all think, act, and communicate
cues.zh: 和世界上的组织，无论是苹果、马丁·路德·金还是莱特兄弟，他们的思考、行动和沟通方式

cues.en: the exact same way,
cues.zh: 完全一样，

cues.en: and it's the complete opposite
cues.zh: 而这与其他人

cues.en: to everyone else.
cues.zh: 恰恰相反。

cues.en: All I did was codify it,
cues.zh: 我所做的只是把它整理提炼了出来，

cues.en: and it's probably the world's simplest idea.
cues.zh: 这大概是世界上最简单的想法了。

cues.en: I call it the golden circle.
cues.zh: 我称它为“黄金圈”。

cues.en: Why,
cues.zh: 为什么、

cues.en: how, what?
cues.zh: 怎么做、做什么？

cues.en: This little idea explains
cues.zh: 这个小小的理念解释了

cues.en: why some organizations and some leaders are able to inspire
cues.zh: 为什么有些组织和领导者能激发人心，

cues.en: where others aren't. Let me define the terms really quickly.
cues.zh: 而其他人却做不到。我先快速定义一下这几个词。

cues.en: Every single person, every single organization on the planet knows what they do 100%.
cues.zh: 地球上的每个人、每个组织，都百分之百清楚自己是“做什么”的。

cues.en: Some
cues.zh: 有些人

cues.en: know how they do it, whether you call it your differentiating value proposition or your proprietary process or your USP.
cues.zh: 知道自己是“怎么做”的，不管你称之为差异化价值主张、专利流程，还是 USP。

cues.en: But very, very few people or organizations
cues.zh: 但极少有人或组织

cues.en: know why they do what they do.
cues.zh: 知道自己“为什么”要做这些。

cues.en: And by why, I don't mean to make a profit.
cues.zh: 这里说的“为什么”，并不是指赚钱。

cues.en: That's a result. It's always a result. By why, I mean what's your purpose? What's your cause? What's your belief?
cues.zh: 赚钱只是结果，从来都只是结果。我说的“为什么”，是指你的目标是什么？使命是什么？信念是什么？

cues.en: Why does your organization
cues.zh: 你的组织为什么

cues.en: exist?
cues.zh: 存在？

cues.en: Why do you get out of bed in the morning?
cues.zh: 你每天早上为什么起床？

cues.en: And why should anyone care?
cues.zh: 别人又凭什么要在乎？

cues.en: Well, as a result, the way we think, the way we act, the way we communicate is from the outside in. It's obvious. We go from the clearest thing to the fuzziest thing.
cues.zh: 所以，我们大多数人思考、行动和沟通的方式，都是由外向内的。这很自然，我们习惯从最清楚的事情走向最模糊的事情。

cues.en: But the inspired leaders and the inspired or inspired organizations,
cues.zh: 但那些鼓舞人心的领袖和卓越组织，

cues.en: regardless of their size, regardless of their industry,
cues.zh: 无论规模多大，无论身处哪个行业，

cues.en: all think, act, and communicate
cues.zh: 思考、行动和沟通的方式，

cues.en: from the inside out.
cues.zh: 全都是由内而外的。

cues.en: Let me give you an example. I use Apple because they're easy to understand and everybody gets it.
cues.zh: 我举个例子。我用 Apple 来说明，因为大家都很熟悉，容易理解。

cues.en: If Apple were like everyone else,
cues.zh: 如果 Apple 也随大流，

cues.en: a marketing message from them might sound like this.
cues.zh: 他们的营销广告听起来大概会是这样：

cues.en: We make great computers.
cues.zh: 我们造很棒的电脑。

cues.en: They're beautifully designed, simple to use, and user friendly.
cues.zh: 它们设计精美、简单易用、用户体验好。

cues.en: Wanna buy one?
cues.zh: 想买一台吗？

cues.en: Meh.
cues.zh: 呃。

cues.en: And that's how most of us communicate.
cues.zh: 我们大多数人就是这么沟通的。

cues.en: Marketing is done, that's how most sales is done, and that's how most of us communicate interpersonally.
cues.zh: 营销是这么做的，大多数销售也是这么做的，我们大多数人的人际沟通也是这么做的。

cues.en: We say what we do, we say how we're different or how we're better, and we expect some sort of behavior, a purchase, a vote, something like that. Here's our new law firm. We have the best lawyers with the biggest clients. We have... You know, we always perform for our clients who do business with us. Here's our new car. It gets great gas mileage. It has, you know, leather seats. Buy our car. But it's uninspiring.
cues.zh: 我们说自己做什么，说自己有何不同、有何优势，然后期待某种行为：购买、投票之类的。这是我们的新律所。我们有最好的律师，服务最大的客户。我们……你知道，我们总是为和我们做生意的客户全力以赴。这是我们的新车。它很省油。它还有，你知道，真皮座椅。买我们的车吧。但这毫无感染力。

cues.en: Here's how Apple actually communicates.
cues.zh: Apple 实际上是这样沟通的。

cues.en: Everything we do,
cues.zh: 我们所做的一切，

cues.en: we believe
cues.zh: 我们相信

cues.en: in challenging the status quo. We believe
cues.zh: 在于挑战现状。我们相信

cues.en: in thinking differently.
cues.zh: 在于不同凡想。

cues.en: The way we challenge the status quo is by making our products beautifully designed, simple to use, and user friendly.
cues.zh: 我们挑战现状的方式，是把产品做得设计精美、简单易用、用户体验好。

cues.en: We just happen to make great computers.
cues.zh: 我们只是恰好造出了很棒的电脑。

cues.en: Wanna buy one?
cues.zh: 想买一台吗？

cues.en: Totally different. Right? You're ready to buy a computer from me. All I did was reverse the order of the information. What it proves to us is that people don't buy what you do, people buy why you do it. People don't buy what you do, they buy why you do it. This explains
cues.zh: 完全不一样，对吧？你已经准备从我这里买电脑了。我只是把信息的顺序倒了过来。它向我们证明：人们买的不是你所做的，而是你为什么这么做。人们买的不是你所做的，而是你为什么这么做。这解释了

cues.en: why every single person in this room
cues.zh: 为什么这个房间里的每一个人

cues.en: is perfectly comfortable buying a computer from Apple.
cues.zh: 都能毫无顾虑地从 Apple 买电脑。

cues.en: But we're also perfectly comfortable buying an m p three player from Apple or a phone from Apple or a DVR from Apple.
cues.zh: 但我们也很乐意买苹果的 MP3 播放器、苹果的手机，或者苹果的 DVR。

cues.en: But as I said before, Apple is just a computer company. There's nothing that distinguishes them structurally from any of their competitors. Their competitors are all equally qualified to make all of these products. In fact, they tried. A few years ago, Gateway came out with flat screen TVs.
cues.zh: 但就像我之前说的，苹果只是一家电脑公司。从结构上讲，他们和任何竞争对手都没有区别。他们的竞争对手同样有资格做出所有这些产品。事实上，他们也尝试过。几年前，Gateway 推出了纯平电视。

cues.en: They're eminently qualified to make flat screen TVs. They've been making flat screen monitors for years.
cues.zh: 他们完全有资格做纯平电视。他们做纯平显示器已经很多年了。

cues.en: Nobody bought one.
cues.zh: 但没人买。

cues.en: And Dell
cues.zh: 还有 Dell

cues.en: Dell came out with m p three players and PDAs.
cues.zh: Dell 推出了 MP3 播放器和 PDA。

cues.en: And they make great quality products, and they can make perfectly well designed products,
cues.zh: 他们做的产品质量很好，也能做出设计精良的产品，

cues.en: and nobody bought one.
cues.zh: 但没人买。

cues.en: In fact, talking about it now, we can't even imagine buying an m p three player from Dell. Why would you buy an m p three player from a computer company? But we do it every day.
cues.zh: 其实现在说起来，我们根本无法想象从 Dell 买 MP3 播放器。你为什么会从一家电脑公司买 MP3 播放器呢？但我们每天都在这么做。

cues.en: People don't buy what you do, they buy why you do it. The goal is not to do business with anybody... With everybody who needs what you have.
cues.zh: 人们买的不是你做什么，而是你为什么做。目标不是和任何需要你产品的人做生意……和所有需要你产品的人。

cues.en: The goal is to do business with people who believe what you believe.
cues.zh: 目标是与那些相信你所相信的人做生意。

cues.en: Here's the best part.
cues.zh: 最精彩的部分来了。

cues.en: None of what I'm telling you is my opinion.
cues.zh: 我告诉你的这些都不是我的个人观点。

cues.en: It's all grounded in the tenets of biology, not psychology,
cues.zh: 这一切都建立在生物学而非心理学的原则之上，

cues.en: biology.
cues.zh: 生物学。

cues.en: If you look at a cross section of the human brain, looking from the top down, what you see is the human brain is actually broken into three major components that correlate perfectly with the golden circle.
cues.zh: 如果你从上往下看人类大脑的横截面，你会看到人类大脑实际上分为三个主要部分，它们与黄金圈完美对应。

cues.en: Our newest brain, our homo sapien brain, our neocortex,
cues.zh: 我们最新的大脑，我们智人的大脑，我们的新皮层，

cues.en: corresponds with the what level? The neocortex is responsible for all of our rational and analytical thought and language.
cues.zh: 对应的是哪个层次？新皮层负责我们所有的理性、分析性思维和语言。

cues.en: The middle two sections make up our limbic brains,
cues.zh: 中间两个部分构成了我们的边缘脑，

cues.en: and our limbic brains are responsible for all of our feelings,
cues.zh: 而我们的边缘脑负责我们所有的感受，

cues.en: like trust
cues.zh: 比如信任

cues.en: and loyalty.
cues.zh: 和忠诚。

cues.en: It's also responsible for all human behavior,
cues.zh: 它还负责所有人类行为、

cues.en: all decision making, and it has no capacity for language.
cues.zh: 所有决策，而且它没有语言能力。

cues.en: In other words, when we communicate from the outside in, yes, people can understand vast amounts of complicated information like features and benefits and facts and figures. It just doesn't drive behavior.
cues.zh: 换句话说，当我们由外而内地沟通时，是的，人们能理解大量复杂信息，比如功能和好处、事实和数据。但它就是无法驱动行为。

cues.en: When we communicate from the inside out, we're talking directly to the part of the brain that controls behavior, and then we allow people to rationalize it with the tangible things we say and do. This is where gut decisions come from.
cues.zh: 当我们由内而外地沟通时，我们是在直接对大脑中控制行为的那部分说话，然后我们让人们用我们所说所做的具体事物去合理化它。直觉决策就是这么来的。

cues.en: You know, sometimes you can give somebody all the facts and figures, you say, I know what all the facts and details say, but it just doesn't feel right. Why would we use that verb? It doesn't feel right. Because the part of the brain that controls decision making doesn't control language. And the best we can muster up is, I don't know, it just doesn't feel right. Or sometimes you say you're leading with your heart, or you're leading with your soul. Well, hate to break it to you, those aren't other body parts controlling your behavior. It's all happening here in your limbic brain, the part of the brain that controls decision making and not language.
cues.zh: 你知道，有时候你给别人摆出所有事实和数据，你说，我知道所有事实和细节怎么说，但就是感觉不对。为什么我们会用那个词？感觉不对。因为控制决策的那部分大脑不控制语言。我们最多只能挤出一句：我不知道，就是感觉不对。或者有时候你说，你是在跟着心走，或者跟着灵魂走。好吧，不想扫你兴，那些并不是控制你行为的其他身体部位。这一切都发生在你的边缘脑里，那是大脑中控制决策、不控制语言的部分。

cues.en: But if you don't know why you do what you do, and people
cues.zh: 但如果你自己都不知道为什么要做这件事，而大家

cues.en: respond to why you do what you do, then how will anybody...
cues.zh: 又恰恰是被你的理念所打动，那别人又怎么会……

cues.en: How will you ever get people to to
cues.zh: 你又怎么可能让大家

cues.en: vote for you or buy something from you, or more importantly,
cues.zh: 给你投票，或者购买你的产品，更重要的是，

cues.en: be loyal, loyal and want to be a part of what it is that you do.
cues.zh: 忠诚于你，并渴望成为你事业的一部分？

cues.en: Again, the goal is not just to sell people who need what you have. The goal is to sell to people who believe what you believe.
cues.zh: 再说一次，目标不仅仅是把东西卖给需要它的人，而是卖给那些相信你所信奉理念的人。

cues.en: The goal is not just to hire people
cues.zh: 招聘的目标也不仅仅是招那些

cues.en: who need a job. It's to hire people who believe what you believe.
cues.zh: 需要一份工作的人，而是招募那些相信你所信奉理念的人。

cues.en: I always say that, you know, this... If you if you if you
cues.zh: 我常说，你看……如果你……如果你

cues.en: hire people just because they can do a job, they'll work for your money. But if you hire people who believe what you believe, they work for you with blood and sweat tears. And nowhere else is there a better example of this than with the Wright brothers.
cues.zh: 招人仅仅是因为他们能干这份活，他们只会为了薪水而工作；但如果你招募的是认同你理念的人，他们就会为你倾注心血、全力以赴。而在这一点上，没有比 Wright brothers 更好的例子了。

cues.en: Most people don't know about Samuel Pierpont Langley. And back in the early twentieth century,
cues.zh: 大多数人都不知道 Samuel Pierpont Langley。在二十世纪初，

cues.en: the pursuit of powered man flight was like the .com of the day. Everybody was trying it. And Samuel Pierpont Langley had what we assume
cues.zh: 探索载人动力飞行就像当年的互联网狂潮（.com）一样，每个人都在尝试。而 Samuel Pierpont Langley 拥有我们所认为的

cues.en: to be the recipe for success.
cues.zh: 成功秘诀。

cues.en: I mean, even now, when you ask people why did your product or why did your company fail, and people always give you the same permutation of the same three things.
cues.zh: 我是说，即使在今天，当你问别人为什么你的产品或公司会失败，他们给出的总是这三个原因的排列组合：

cues.en: Undercapitalized,
cues.zh: 资金不足、

cues.en: the wrong people, bad market conditions, it's always the same three things. So let's explore that.
cues.zh: 用人不当、市场行情不好，永远都是这三点。那么我们不妨来探究一下。

cues.en: Samuel Pierpont Langley
cues.zh: Samuel Pierpont Langley

cues.en: was given $50,000
cues.zh: 拿到了 5 万美元

cues.en: by the war department to figure out this flying machine. Money was no problem. He held a seat at Harvard and worked at the Smithsonian,
cues.zh: 由战争部拨款，让他研制飞行器。钱不是问题。他在哈佛有教职，还在史密森尼学会工作，

cues.en: and was extremely well connected. He knew all the big minds of the day. He hired the best minds money could find,
cues.zh: 而且人脉极广。他认识当时所有的大人物。他雇得起最好的头脑，

cues.en: and the market conditions were fantastic.
cues.zh: 市场条件也非常理想。

cues.en: The New York Times followed him around everywhere, and everyone was rooting for Langley.
cues.zh: 《纽约时报》到处跟着他报道，所有人都看好 Langley。

cues.en: And how come we've never heard of Samuel Pierpont Langley?
cues.zh: 可为什么我们从没听说过 Samuel Pierpont Langley？

cues.en: A few 100 miles away in Dayton, Ohio,
cues.zh: 几百英里外的俄亥俄州代顿市，

cues.en: Orville and Wilbur Wright.
cues.zh: Orville 和 Wilbur Wright。

cues.en: They had none
cues.zh: 他们完全没有

cues.en: of what we consider to be the recipe for success. They had no money. They paid for their dream with the proceeds from their bicycle shop. Not a single person on the Wright brothers team had a college education, not even Orville or Wilbur. And the New York Times followed them around nowhere.
cues.zh: 我们所认为的成功要素。他们没钱。他们用自行车店的收入来供养自己的梦想。Wright 兄弟团队里没有一个人上过大学，连 Orville 和 Wilbur 都没有。《纽约时报》也从来不去跟他们的报道。

cues.en: The difference was Orville and Wilbur were driven by a cause, by a purpose, by a belief. They believed that if they could figure out this flying machine,
cues.zh: 区别在于，Orville 和 Wilbur 是被一份事业、一个目标、一种信念驱动的。他们相信，只要能造出这台飞行器，

cues.en: it'll change the course of the world.
cues.zh: 就能改变世界的进程。

cues.en: Samuel Pierpont Langley was different. He wanted to be rich, and he wanted to be famous. He was in pursuit of the result. He was in pursuit of the riches.
cues.zh: Samuel Pierpont Langley 则不同。他想发财，也想出名。他追求的是结果。他追求的是财富。

cues.en: And lo and behold, look what happened. The people who believed
cues.zh: 结果你猜怎么着？那些相信

cues.en: in the Wright brothers' dream worked with them with blood and sweat and tears. The others just worked for the paycheck.
cues.zh: Wright 兄弟梦想的人，与他们并肩奋斗，流血流汗流泪。其他人只是为了薪水工作。

cues.en: And they tell stories of how every time the Wright brothers went out, they would have to take five sets of parts, because that's how many times they would crash before they came in for supper.
cues.zh: 他们说，Wright 兄弟每次出去，都得带五套零件，因为他们要摔这么多次，才能回来吃晚饭。

cues.en: And eventually, on December seventeenth nineteen o three,
the Wright brothers took flight,
cues.zh: Wright 兄弟飞上了天，

cues.en: and no one was there to even experience it. We found out about it a few days later.
cues.zh: 甚至没有人在场经历这一刻。我们是几天后才知道的。

cues.en: And further proof that Langley was motivated by the wrong thing,
cues.zh: 还有进一步证据表明，Langley 是被错误的东西驱动的：

cues.en: the day the Wright brothers took flight,
cues.zh: 就在 Wright 兄弟试飞成功那天，

cues.en: he quit.
cues.zh: 他放弃了。

cues.en: He could have said, that's an amazing discovery guys, and I will improve upon your technology.
cues.zh: 他本可以说，伙计们，这是惊人的发现，我会改进你们的技术。

cues.en: But he didn't. He wasn't first, he didn't get rich, he didn't get famous,
cues.zh: 但他没有。他不是第一个，他没赚到钱，也没出名，

cues.en: so he quit.
cues.zh: 所以他放弃了。

cues.en: People don't buy what you do, they buy why you do it. And if you talk about what you believe,
cues.zh: 人们买的不是你做的什么，而是你为什么做。如果你谈论你所相信的，

cues.en: you will attract those who believe what you believe.
cues.zh: 你就会吸引那些相信你所相信的人。

cues.en: Well, why is it important to attract those who believe what you believe?
cues.zh: 那么，为什么吸引那些相信你所相信的人很重要？

cues.en: Something called the law of diffusion of innovation. And if you don't know the law, you definitely know the terminology.
cues.zh: 有个东西叫创新扩散定律。如果你不知道这条定律，你肯定知道这个术语。

cues.en: The first two and a half percent of our population are our innovators.
cues.zh: 我们人口中前2.5%是创新者。

cues.en: The next 13 and a half percent of our population are our early adopters.
cues.zh: 接下来13.5%是早期采用者。

cues.en: The next 34% are your early majority, your late majority, and your laggards.
cues.zh: 接下来34%是早期大众、晚期大众和落后者。

cues.en: The only reason these people buy touch tone phones is because you can't buy rotary phones anymore.
cues.zh: 这些人买按键式电话的唯一原因，是你再也买不到转盘式电话了。

cues.en: We all sit at various places at various times on the scale, but what the law of diffusion of innovation tells us is that if you want mass market success or mass market acceptance of an idea,
cues.zh: 我们都会在不同时间处于这条曲线上的不同位置，但创新扩散定律告诉我们，如果你想让一个想法获得大众市场的成功或大众市场的认可，

cues.en: you cannot have it until you achieve
cues.zh: 你就无法实现，直到你达到

cues.en: this tipping point between 1518%
cues.zh: 这个15%到18%之间的临界点，

cues.en: market penetration,
cues.zh: 市场渗透率，

cues.en: and then the system tips.
cues.zh: 然后整个系统就会翻转。

cues.en: And I love asking businesses, what's your conversion on new business? And they love to tell you, oh, it's about 10% proudly. Well, you can trip over 10% of the customers. We all have about 10% who just get it. That's how we describe them. Right? That's like that gut feeling. Oh, they just get it. The problem is how do you find the ones that just get it before you're doing business with them, versus the ones who don't get it.
cues.zh: 我喜欢问企业，你们新业务的转化率是多少？他们很爱自豪地告诉你，哦，大约10%。可10%的客户，你随便都能碰到。我们都有大约10%的人就是“懂”。我们就是这么形容他们的。对吧？就像那种直觉。哦，他们就是懂。问题在于，你如何在和他们做生意之前，找到那些“懂”的人，而不是那些不懂的人。

cues.en: So, it's this here, this little gap
cues.zh: 所以，就是这里，这个小缺口

cues.en: that you have to close, as Jeffrey Moore calls it, Crossing
cues.zh: 你必须弥合它，正如杰弗里·摩尔所说的，跨越

cues.en: the Chasm. Because you see, the early majority will not try something until someone else
cues.zh: 鸿沟。因为你看，早期大众不会尝试某样东西，直到别人

cues.en: has tried it first.
cues.zh: 先试过。

cues.en: And these guys, the innovators and the early adopters, they're comfortable making those gut decisions. They're more comfortable making those intuitive decisions that are driven by what they believe about the world,
cues.zh: 而这些人，创新者和早期采用者，他们乐于做那种直觉决策。他们更愿意做那种由他们对世界的信念驱动的直觉判断，

cues.en: and not just what product is available. These are the people who stood online for six hours to buy an iPhone when they first came out, when you could have just walked into the store the next week and bought one off the shelf. These are the people who spent $40,000
cues.zh: 而不只是看有什么产品可用。这些人会在iPhone刚问世时排队六小时去买，而其实你下周走进店里就能从货架上买一台。这些人会花4万美元

cues.en: on flat screen TVs when they first came out, even though the technology was substandard.
cues.zh: 去买刚问世的平板电视，尽管当时技术还不达标。

cues.en: And by the way, they didn't do it because the technology was so great.
cues.zh: 顺便说一句，他们这么做并不是因为这项技术有多出色。

cues.en: They did it for themselves.
cues.zh: 他们是为了自己。

cues.en: It's because they wanted to be first.
cues.zh: 因为他们想成为第一。

cues.en: People don't buy what you do, they buy why you do it. And what you do simply proves what you believe.
cues.zh: 人们买的不是你做什么，而是你为什么这么做。而你做什么，只是证明了你的信念。

cues.en: In fact, people will do the things that prove what they believe.
cues.zh: 事实上，人们会做那些能够证明自己信念的事情。

cues.en: The reason that person bought the iPhone in the first six
cues.zh: 那个人之所以在前六

cues.en: hours, or stood in line for six hours,
cues.zh: 个小时内买下 iPhone，或者排队等了六个小时，

cues.en: was because they believed about the world and how they wanted everybody to see them. They were first.
cues.zh: 是因为他们对这个世界有自己的看法，也希望所有人都这样看他们。他们是第一。

cues.en: People don't buy what you do, they buy why you do it. So let me give you a famous example, a famous failure and a famous success of the law of diffusion of innovation.
cues.zh: 人们买的不是你做什么，而是你为什么这么做。所以，我来举一个创新扩散定律的著名失败案例和著名成功案例。

cues.en: First, the famous failure.
cues.zh: 先说这个著名的失败案例。

cues.en: It's a commercial example.
cues.zh: 这是一个商业案例。

cues.en: As we said before a second ago, the recipe for success is money, and the right people, and the right market conditions. Right? You should have success then.
cues.zh: 正如我们刚才说过的，成功的秘诀是资金、合适的人，以及合适的市场环境。对吧？这样你应该就能成功了。

cues.en: Look at TiVo.
cues.zh: 看看 TiVo。

cues.en: From the time TiVo came out, about eight or nine years ago, to this current day, they are the single highest quality product on the market. Hands down, there is no dispute.
cues.zh: 从 TiVo 大约八九年前推出，一直到今天，它一直是市场上质量最高的产品。毫无疑问，没有争议。

cues.en: They were extremely well funded. Market conditions were fantastic. I mean, we use TiVo as a verb. I TiVo stuff on my piece of junk Time Warner DVR all the time.
cues.zh: 他们的资金非常充足，市场环境也非常好。我的意思是，我们甚至把 TiVo 当作动词用。我总是在我的破 Time Warner DVR 上 TiVo 东西。

cues.en: But TiVo's a commercial failure.
cues.zh: 但 TiVo 是一个商业上的失败案例。

cues.en: They've never made money.
cues.zh: 他们从来没赚到钱。

cues.en: And when they went IPO,
cues.zh: 而且当他们进行 IPO 时，

cues.en: their stock was at about 30 or $40, then plummeted, and it's never traded above 10. In fact, I don't think it's even traded above 6, except for a couple of little spikes.
cues.zh: 他们的股价大约是 30 到 40 美元，之后一路暴跌，再也没涨到 10 美元以上。事实上，除了几次短暂的尖峰，我觉得它甚至都没涨到 6 美元以上。

cues.en: Because you see, when TiVo launched their product, they told us all what they had.
cues.zh: 因为你看，TiVo推出产品时，他们告诉大家他们有什么。

cues.en: They said, we have a product that pauses live TV,
cues.zh: 他们说，我们有一款产品，可以暂停直播电视，

cues.en: skips commercials,
cues.zh: 跳过广告，

cues.en: rewinds live TV, and memorizes your viewing habits without you even asking.
cues.zh: 回看直播电视，还能在你没要求的情况下记住你的观看习惯。

cues.en: And the cynical majority said, we don't believe you.
cues.zh: 而愤世嫉俗的大多数人说，我们不信你。

cues.en: We don't need it. We don't like it, you're scaring us.
cues.zh: 我们不需要它。我们不喜欢它，你吓到我们了。

cues.en: What if they had said, if you're the kind of person
cues.zh: 如果他们当时说，如果你是那种

cues.en: who likes to have total control
cues.zh: 喜欢完全掌控

cues.en: over every aspect of your life,
cues.zh: 生活方方面面的人，

cues.en: boy, do we have a product for you.
cues.zh: 天哪，我们正好有一款产品适合你。

cues.en: It pauses live TV, skips commercials, memorizes your viewing habits, etcetera, etcetera.
cues.zh: 它能暂停直播电视、跳过广告、记住你的观看习惯，等等等等。

cues.en: People don't buy what you do, they buy why you do it, and what you do simply serves as the proof
cues.zh: 人们买的不是你做什么，而是你为什么做，你做什么只是作为证明

cues.en: of what you believe.
cues.zh: 你所相信的东西。

cues.en: Now, let me give you a successful example of the law of diffusion of innovation.
cues.zh: 现在，让我给你一个创新扩散定律的成功例子。

cues.en: In the summer of nineteen sixty three,
people showed up on the mall in Washington to hear doctor King speak.
cues.zh: 人聚集在华盛顿的国家广场，听金博士演讲。

cues.en: They sent out no invitations,
cues.zh: 他们没有发出任何邀请，

cues.en: and there was no website to check the date.
cues.zh: 也没有网站可以查日期。

cues.en: How do you do that?
cues.zh: 你是怎么做到的？

cues.en: Well,
cues.zh: 嗯，

cues.en: doctor King wasn't the only man in America who was the... Who was a great orator. He wasn't the only man in America who suffered in a pre civil rights America. In fact, some of his ideas were bad,
cues.zh: 金博士并不是美国唯一一个……唯一一个伟大的演说家。他也不是美国唯一一个在民权运动之前的美国受苦的人。事实上，他的一些想法并不好，

cues.en: but he had a gift.
cues.zh: 但他有一种天赋。

cues.en: He didn't go around telling people what needed to change in America. He went around and told people what he believed.
cues.zh: 他没有到处告诉人们美国需要改变什么。他到处告诉人们他所相信的是什么。

cues.en: I believe.
cues.zh: 我相信。

cues.en: Believe. I believe, he told people.
cues.zh: 相信。我相信，他对人们说。

cues.en: And people who believed what he believed
cues.zh: 而那些相信他所相信的人

cues.en: took his cause and they made it their own, and they told people.
cues.zh: 接受了他的事业，把它变成自己的事业，并把这份信念告诉更多人。

cues.en: And some of those people created
cues.zh: 其中一些人建立了

cues.en: structures to get the word out to even more people.
cues.zh: 各种组织，把这个消息传递给更多人。

cues.en: And lo and behold,
cues.zh: 结果你看，
25万人

cues.en: people showed up on the right day, on the right time to hear him speak.
cues.zh: 在正确的日子、正确的时间赶到现场，听他演讲。

cues.en: How many of them showed up for him?
cues.zh: 他们有多少人是为了他来的？

cues.en: Zero.
cues.zh: 一个也没有。

cues.en: They showed up for themselves.
cues.zh: 他们是为了自己而来。

cues.en: It's what they believed about America that got them to travel on a bus for eight hours to stand in the sun in Washington for... In the middle of August. It's what they believed, and it wasn't about black versus white. 25% of the audience was white.
cues.zh: 正是他们对美国的信念，让他们坐八个小时的公交车，在八月中旬的华盛顿烈日下站立……他们所相信的，并不是黑人和白人之间的对立。现场有25%的听众是白人。

cues.en: Doctor King believed that there are two types of laws in this world, those that are made by a higher authority and those that are made by man. And not until all the laws that are made by man
cues.zh: King博士相信，这个世界上有两种法律：一种由更高的权威制定，另一种由人制定。只有等到所有由人制定的法律

cues.en: are consistent with the laws that are made by the higher authority will we live in a just world.
cues.zh: 都符合更高权威制定的法律时，我们才会生活在一个公正的世界。

cues.en: It just so happens that the civil rights movement was the perfect thing to help him bring his cause to life.
cues.zh: 恰好，民权运动是帮助他让自己的事业落地的完美契机。

cues.en: We followed not him, not for him, but for ourselves.
cues.zh: 我们追随的不是他，也不是为了他，而是为了我们自己。

cues.en: And by the way, he gave the I have a dream speech, not the I have a plan speech.
cues.zh: 顺便说一句，他发表的是“我有一个梦想”的演讲，而不是“我有一个计划”的演讲。

cues.en: Listen to politicians now with their comprehensive 12 plans, they're not inspiring anybody.
cues.zh: 听听现在的政客，他们拿出一套套全面的十二点计划，却没有激励任何人。

cues.en: Because there are leaders and there are those who lead.
cues.zh: 因为世上有领导者，也有真正能够带领他人的人。

cues.en: Leaders hold a position of power or authority,
cues.zh: 领导者拥有权力或权威的地位，

cues.en: but those who lead
cues.zh: 但那些真正引领的人

cues.en: inspire us.
cues.zh: 激励着我们。

cues.en: Whether they're individuals or organizations,
cues.zh: 无论他们是个人还是组织，

cues.en: we follow those who lead,
cues.zh: 我们追随那些引领的人，

cues.en: not because we have to,
cues.zh: 不是因为我们不得不，

cues.en: but because we want to.
cues.zh: 而是因为我们愿意。

cues.en: We follow those who lead, not for them,
cues.zh: 我们追随那些引领的人，不是为了他们，

cues.en: but for ourselves.
cues.zh: 而是为了我们自己。

cues.en: And it's those who start with why
cues.zh: 而那些从“为什么”出发的人

cues.en: that have the ability
cues.zh: 才有能力

cues.en: to inspire those around them, or find others who inspire them.
cues.zh: 去激励身边的人，或者找到能激励自己的人。

cues.en: Thank you very much.
cues.zh: 非常感谢。

cues.en: Sharing.
cues.zh: 分享。

cues.en: That's video on the human network.
cues.zh: 这就是“人类网络”的视频。

cues.en: Cisco,
cues.zh: Cisco，

cues.en: welcome to the human network.
cues.zh: 欢迎来到人类网络。
